correctness.rationale: Green–Stokes and L1 approximation identify normalized T_r=J_r/(2πir²) with disk averaging of ∂bar f in locally integrable/distribution senses. Distributional convergence T_r→∂bar f plus locally uniform L1 boundedness exactly characterizes a locally finite complex Radon derivative via order-zero Riesz representation. If µ=∂bar f is a Radon measure, triangle+Tonelli provide limsup ∫φ|κ_r*µ|≤∫φ d|µ|; weak measure convergence and weighted total-variation lower semicontinuity provide reverse liminf. Hence |T_r|dA⇀|µ| and continuity-set masses converge. Decompose µ=h dA+µ_s: measure differentiation gives a.e. disk-average h, κ_r*h→h in local L1, so ∫E|T_r-h|→|µ_s|(E), with boundary-null condition. Cantor distribution constructed with ℓ_n=2^-n(n+1)^-β has zero-length support, near-Lipschitz logarithmic modulus, nonzero singular derivative, and is locally constant at a.e. center. Lipschitz data have absolutely continuous derivative; a.e. vanishing then implies holomorphic. Explicit f=bar z and bar z² fix normalization.

originality.rationale: Guo–Xiao 2026 primary full text (6 pages) proves that continuous f with o(r²) circular integrals at every center is holomorphic, but does not address Radon measure characterization, strict recovery of derivative variation, or exact singular residual. A distinct published averaged-Morera result works with L1 distributional convergence and averaged vanishing, also weaker than total-variation recovery. General strict approximation of Radon measures by positive kernels is known and is explicitly NOT claimed novel; the mathematically motivated application is the complete Morera-defect endpoint diagnostic and its singular-vs-pointwise contrast.
residual_risks: A general BV/Radon-measure treatment could explicitly formulate the same disk-boundary diagnostic under older terminology.
Full primary averaged-Morera record was not independently obtained; only its available description was compared.
Canonical disk-average representative is required for simultaneous radius-wise a.e. convergence; arbitrary circle representatives are not.

value.rationale: The circular Morera problem asks what the family of local circular integrals detects. This theorem sharpens mere holomorphy detection to exact measurement of complex derivative variation and singular mass for L1 data, with near-Lipschitz counterexamples exhibiting failure of pointwise-a.e. tests. It organizes a meaningful endpoint regularity boundary, not just a tautological normalization.

limitations: Only local L1 data, local measures, a.e. centers and boundary-null sets for sharp unweighted mass limit.
No rate of variation convergence; logarithmic-Hölder counterexamples do not contradict everywhere-centered Morera.
